_source: ADR 4.3.3/4.3.4 (API field: adrTankCode, Table A column 12) — PARTIALLY OMITTED by design: the full, very extensive "rational use" tables (assigning every combination of class/classification code/packing group to a specific tank code) were NOT reproduced in full — too voluminous as tabular data. What is reproduced is the code decoding structure, the hierarchy rule, and the complete list of substances with an individually assigned tank code (marked "(+)" in column 12).

code_structure.description: The ADR tank code consists of 4 parts in a fixed order, e.g. "L4BH".

part_1_type.L: tanks for liquid substances (or solids carried in the molten state)

part_2_calculation_pressure.G: minimum calculation pressure per the general requirements of 6.8.2.1.14

part_3_openings.C: top openings for filling and discharge, with only cleaning openings below the surface of the liquid
part_3_openings.D: top openings, with no openings below the surface of the liquid

part_4_valves_safety_equipment.V: breather device per 6.8.2.2.6, without a flame arrester, or tank not resistant to explosion pressure shock
part_4_valves_safety_equipment.F: breather device per 6.8.2.2.6 with a flame arrester, or tank resistant to explosion pressure shock
part_4_valves_safety_equipment.N: without a breather device per 6.8.2.2.6, not hermetically closed

tank_hierarchy.rule: A tank bearing a code other than the one indicated for a given substance may be used if each of the 4 parts of the code corresponds to a safety level at least equivalent to (or higher than) that of the assigned code, per the ascending hierarchy below — this does not, however, take account of special provisions for individual entries (see 4.3.5, 6.8.4).
tank_hierarchy.example: a tank coded L10CN is permitted for a substance requiring L4BN; a tank coded L4BN is permitted for a substance requiring SGAN.

individual_assignments_plus._description: Substances marked "(+)" in Table A column 12 have an individually assigned, mandatory tank code; alternative tanks are permitted only if specified in the type-approval certificate, or tanks with a higher code value per the hierarchy plus the special provisions in column 13.

un_examples.UN 2015 hydrogen peroxide, stabilized, >: L4DV (or L4BV — see variants in the source table)
un_examples.UN 2014 hydrogen peroxide 20–60%, UN 242: L4BV / LGAV (depending on the specific entry)
un_examples.class_7 (radioactive material): special tanks; minimum requirements: liquids L2.65CN, solids S2.65AN (tanks for radioactive material may also be used for other goods under the conditions of 5.1.3.2)

individual_assignments_plus.tanks_for_liquid_wastes: Tanks complying with Chapter 6.10 (two closures per 6.10.3.2) — code L4AH; if they allow alternating carriage of liquids and solids, a combined code L4AH+S4AH.

_note_rational_use: The full 4.3.4.1.2 tables assigning every combination of class/classification code/packing group to a specific tank code (e.g. LGAV, LGBV, LGBF, L1.5BN, L4BN, L4BH, L10BH, L10CH, L10DH, L15CH, L21DH, SGAV, SGAN, SGAH, S4AH, S10AN, S10AH) have been omitted — too extensive as tabular data. In practice, the adrTankCode field returned by the API already gives the correct/required code for a given UN number, so these tables are mainly needed to verify alternative tanks, which the hierarchy rule above already covers.
